newsitem.title: USA: Ascent, Denver agree on arena.
newsitem.headline: Ascent, Denver agree on arena.

text.p: The city of Denver and Ascent Entertainment Group said on Tuesday they reached an agreement to build a sports arena on a 50 acre site that will keep the Denver Nuggets basketball team and the Colorado Avalanche hockey team in Denver for 25 years.
Denver-based Ascent owns the two sports teams. The Pepsi Center arena is expected to be completed in time for the 1999/2000 season, officials said.
Under the agreement that took three years to negotiate, the estimated $165 million total construction cost would be privately financed by Ascent.
Mayor Wellington Webb called the agreement a "good deal for the city."
A sticking point had been what to do with McNichols Sports Arena, a city-owned venue where the two teams are under contract to play.
Under the agreement, the city retains control of McNichols and if it decides to demolish it within four years after the new arena is opened, Ascent will contribute toward the demolition costs.

Contracts underlying the agreement must be approved by the city counsel, which is expected to take several months City Council President Cathy Reynolds said after the agreement was announced at city hall.
Ascent Chief Executive Officer Charlie Lyons said the company could not obtain financing until the deal was finalized, but that Bear Stearns had been retained.
Ascent also agreed to pay prevailing wages to construction workers who build the arena, a key point for the city.
